findings.location: publishPackageFiles, the existing-output-directory branch (rm(outputDirectory, { recursive: false, force: false }))
findings.problem: The branch is written to tolerate an output directory that already exists and is empty: it lstats the path, rejects symlinks and non-directories, rejects a non-empty directory, and otherwise removes the directory before renaming staging into place. The removal call passes recursive: false, and Node's fs.rm throws ERR_FS_EISDIR on a directory regardless of whether it is empty. I reproduced this directly by executing fs/promises.rm on a fresh empty directory in the declared scratch path: 'Path is a directory: rm returned EISDIR (is a directory)'. The surrounding catch re-throws anything whose code is not ENOENT, so the thrown EISDIR propagates and materializeMeetingDashboardPackage exits 1. The intended empty-directory path is therefore dead: only the absent-directory (ENOENT) path can ever succeed. In this run the output path did not pre-exist, so preserved validator 3 recorded exit status 0; the defect is latent, not triggered. Its practical effect is that the packaging command is not re-runnable once artifacts/current/client-meeting-dashboard-builder/ exists in any form, which will consume an attempt in any unattended re-arm of this playbook. Severity is Low because the failure is fail-closed and loud: staging is removed in the finally block, so no partial or stale package can ever be published.
findings.proposed_fix: Pass { recursive: true, force: false } to the rm call for the verified-empty directory, or drop the removal entirely and rename the staging directory over the empty target after the emptiness check. Add a regression test that pre-creates an empty output directory and asserts the materialization still succeeds.

findings.location: document head; four external asset references
findings.problem: dashboard.html is a post-hydration DOM capture of the served page, byte-identical (sha256 62b82aed71b4a5733b8354ea935d67093884ed5e66ebaedf5e7e05a7e20ee98a) to artifacts/user-smoke/page-source.html. That makes it an honest capture, but it is not self-contained: it references /assets/index-D0F8Jmyk.js, /assets/react-vendor-BBQvgbyt.js, /assets/echarts-DhfVT81Y.js, and /assets/index-Bp6GjY7z.css, none of which is among the six package parts. Opened outside the serving app, the document loses styling and interactivity. The governance content survives that loss, which is why this is Low and not higher: the synthetic disclosure, the upstream digest, the twelve claim-source citations, the KPI values, the tables, and the ECharts SVG are all inline in the captured markup, and the document contains no sr-only, display:none, or display: none rule that would hide anything once the stylesheet is absent.
findings.proposed_fix: Either inline the built CSS and drop the script references when capturing the package copy of dashboard.html, or ship the referenced /assets/ files as additional package parts and document that dashboard.html must be served from the package root.

findings.location: IDLE_WAREHOUSE_WORK_PACKAGE_DIGEST constant, and the absence of any hashing primitive in the scoped surface
findings.problem: The upstream digest that the entire package cites is a hardcoded string constant compared by string equality against the dashboard manifest; it is never derived from bytes anywhere in the scoped dataflow. A search of frontend/src and frontend/package-tools for createHash, subtle.digest, or any equivalent returns nothing, and the SyntheticDataArtifactAdapter comment states this is deliberate ('the canonical Python rfpf envelope is verified before this record reaches DashForge; TypeScript deliberately does not parse or reconstruct that envelope'). Consequently, if the vendored fixtures under frontend/src/fixtures/dataforge/ ever drifted from the received receipt files, no product code would detect it. In this run nothing has drifted: I compared all four fixtures to the corresponding received files by parsed-value equality and each is exactly equal, and I recomputed all 16 external byte pins (12 file_hash_matches in playbooks/shakedown_client_meeting_dashboard_builder.yaml plus 4 receipt received_files entries) and all 16 hold. Note also that the canonical digest sha256:57ed2966... is not the plain file hash of work-package.json, which is sha256:00768e3a...; it is an Agent-Orch canonicalization asserted by the receipt and the envelope. I attempted several plain-JSON canonicalizations of the payload and of the envelope-plus-payload object and reproduced none of them, so the canonical form is not independently re-derivable from the scoped surface.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a build- or test-time check that hashes each fixture under frontend/src/fixtures/dataforge/ against the receipt's received_files map, so fixture drift fails a test rather than passing silently on a hardcoded constant.

findings.problem: The required-surface rule covers every widget, the dashboard description, the five standard story-arc surfaces, the executive summary, and any declared additionalMaterialSurfaceIds, but never narrative.presenterNotes. Those notes ship inside the packaged dashboard.spec.json and are rendered by presenter mode, so they are material text that reaches a human audience while being structurally exempt from claim coverage; nothing would block readiness if a future note asserted a number. Severity is Low because the three notes currently shipped are generic delivery coaching ('Open with the main client outcome before reading the chart.', 'Pause after the tension section to confirm the room sees the same risk.', 'Close by naming the decision this prototype is meant to support.'), assert nothing about the data, and appear nowhere in dashboard.html.
findings.proposed_fix: Either add a narrative:presenter-notes surface (or one surface per note) to collectRequiredMaterialSurfaceIds, or add an explicit schema constraint documenting that presenter notes must not carry data assertions, with a test covering the constraint.

findings.location: the standalone-dashboard-stage section; the five dashboard-box widget cards
findings.problem: Twelve of the eighteen ledger surfaces render a visible standalone-claim-source line in the delivered document (the four metric evidence cards, the two recommendation entries, the five story-arc storyboard sections, and the dashboard description). The five dashboard-stage widget cards - Monthly Opportunity (High), Idle Warehouse Count, Warehouse Credit Concentration, Warehouse Control Gaps, and Prioritized Recommendations - render their values, chart, and tables with no on-surface source line, even though widget:* surfaces are individually cited in the claim ledger. This is not a coverage violation and does not weaken the readiness gate: the ledger covers all 18 required surfaces, and the same underlying numbers appear with citations in the evidence section above the stage. It is a presentation gap - a client reading the dashboard stage alone sees governed numbers without their citation.
findings.proposed_fix: Render a ClaimCitation for each widget surface in the standalone dashboard stage, reusing findMaterialClaim(spec, `widget:${widget.id}`), so every visible governed number carries its source inline.

claim_coverage_enforcement.justification: Enforcement is layered and load-bearing: collectRequiredMaterialSurfaceIds derives the required set from the spec, validateMaterialClaimCoverage requires a claim per surface and rejects duplicate ids, duplicate surfaces, and wrong-digest citations, validateClaimLedger additionally resolves each claim's dataset, fields, and predicate against actual snapshot rows, createDashboardGenerationResult folds all of it into status, and createMeetingDashboardPackageParts emits nothing unless status is ready with zero errors. I recomputed the required set independently at 18 surfaces and the ledger carries exactly 18 claims across 18 distinct surfaces, all citing the correct digest, with empty set difference in both directions. The two findings are a structural exemption (presenter notes) and a presentation gap (uncited widget cards), neither of which breaks coverage.
